explanation: The islands lie closer to Myanmar and Indonesia than to the Indian mainland. Their main town is more than 1,300 km from Chennai.

claims.text: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands belong to India.
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are not part of Myanmar, Thailand or Indonesia.
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie closer to Myanmar and Indonesia than to mainland India.
Port Blair is more than 1,300 km from Chennai.
Port Blair is the main town of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check reports no errors and one C22 warning: the same answer as p.sport.0113, which asks where snakes and ladders began, a different fact; related, not a duplicate, for the editor to confirm with related_ok. Claims: every checkable statement is listed, distractors included; c1 (checker_doubt) and c4 (number) are high under the C26 floor, and c2, c3 and c5 are standard. Datasets: geonames-cities: Port Blair, IN, 11.66613, 92.74635 (c1). Great-circle distances from those coordinates: Chennai, IN, 13.08784, 80.27847, about 1,363 km (c4); Pathein, MM, 16.77919, 94.73212, about 607 km; Banda Aceh, ID, 5.54167, 95.33333, about 738 km (c3). Rival test: Myanmar is the planted trap, much closer and across the Andaman Sea; Thailand faces the islands to the east, and Indonesia's Sumatra lies just south of the Nicobars. Against the key: nothing; the islands are an Indian union territory. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: South Asian players have an edge, as with any place question, but most players worldwide meet the islands only on a map. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight apostrophes, explanation of 25 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no entry matches. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. External evidence: none beyond the dataset; the key is high only because the item is counterintuitive. Seed: 5 (hard): most players pick by distance and miss it; reasoners recall Port Blair or the islands' Indian names. Counterintuitive: true; the obvious answer is wrong, as the rival test explains, and the explanation defuses it. Doubts: c1 is high under the C26 floor because the item is counterintuitive; the schema's riskReason list has no 'counterintuitive', so checker_doubt stands in.

This rests on my knowledge: the shared WebSearch budget was used up before I could attach a source, and geonames-cities 1.1.65 still lists Port Blair, so the editor should confirm it with a web result.

claimResults.note: GeoNames lists the territory as a first-level division of India (country code IN), and its places in cities.json carry country IN and admin1 01, for example {"name":"Port Blair","lat":"11.66613","lng":"92.74635","country":"IN","admin1":"01","admin2":"640"}. world-cities agrees (Port Blair,India,Andaman and Nicobar,1259385), but it is built from GeoNames, so it is no independent second source. High risk (checker_doubt): this dataset record is the external evidence. Cold solve India, high confidence.

claimResults.note: Haversine on GeoNames coordinates (mean Earth radius 6,371 km), nearest pair over all nine IN.01 places: nearest mainland Indian place 981 km (Diglipur to Parva I; Lakshadweep, IN.14, left out as islands), nearest Myanmar place 372 km (Diglipur to Labutta), nearest Indonesian place 200 km (Campbell Bay to Sabang). From Port Blair itself: 1,158 km to the nearest mainland place (Konārka, Odisha), 544 km to Labutta, 702 km to Sabang. Towns stand in for coastlines, but the margins are wide.

Great-circle distance from these coordinates by haversine (mean Earth radius 6,371 km): 1,363 km. A straight line is the shortest possible distance, so any sea or air route is longer still, and 'more than 1,300 km' holds with about 60 km to spare. High risk (number): this dataset record is the external evidence.

evidence.restatement: Port Blair, on South Andaman, is the capital and largest town of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; India renamed it Sri Vijaya Puram in September 2024.

claimResults.note: No web search ran: the shared turn-wide WebSearch budget was exhausted (my one call was refused before it ran), so this rests on knowledge. The pinned city datasets list Port Blair in the territory but carry no capital flag or population (world-cities only says each of its four rows has 15,000 people or more). Standard risk.

issues.note: Myanmar's Coco Islands lie just north of North Andaman on the same island chain, but they are not part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Indian union territory the stem names. A player who knows them still answers India, so Myanmar is no second answer.

India renamed Port Blair Sri Vijaya Puram in September 2024 (my knowledge; no search could run). Claims c4 and c5 use the old name, but the player-facing explanation says only 'their main town', so nothing a player sees is out of date. If the town is ever named in player-facing text, use 'Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair)'.
